title: Data Sovereignty Contractual Exception Workbench
content:
Purpose:
This is a working "workbench" for handling customer contractual exceptions to standard data residency commitments. It collects the cross-functional checklist, lightweight risk mitigations we can apply immediately, evidence artifacts to attach to a contract, and a small SRE/legal playbook for temporary exceptions (waivers or transitional allowances).

Context / why this exists:
- Increasingly enterprise customers ask for temporary or scoped exceptions that contradict our default territory commitments (e.g., dev logs routed through a partner region, or onboarding where customer needs short-term temporary processing outside their target jurisdiction).
- We need a repeatable, low-friction process to evaluate, accept, and operationalize such exceptions with minimal SLO/regulatory risk.
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic & prescriptive — not a policy doc; the goal is to accelerate consistent decisions and generate reproducible audit evidence.

Quick definitions (working):
- Exception: any contract clause or operational request that lets customer data be processed or stored outside the standard pinned region for that tenant.
- Temporary waiver: time-limited exception with explicit expiry and required mitigations.
- Scoped exception: an exception gated to certain data classes, API endpoints, or admin roles.

Decision triage (fast path):
1) Intake (sales/SE) — capture request with minimal fields: customer, account id, requested deviation, business justification, requested dates. Create INF-xxxx in Jira using template "ds-exception-intake".
2) Legal review (T+48h) — legal tags: allowed? need amendment? insurance? policy note.
3) Technical gating (SRE/Private Deployments) — can we implement isolation & telemetry? what mitigations?
4) Risk owner assigns: product security or eng-ops.
5) If low-risk + time-limited -> proceed via waiver template. If high-risk -> require contract amendment + exec approval.

Minimum technical mitigations (apply in parallel):
- Isolation boundary: ensure data and KV caches are scoped to tenant and separated from other territories. Document the isolation path (service names, cluster ids).
- Encryption at rest with customer KMS where possible; if not, scoped HSM note plus compensating controls.
- Access controls: restrict operator-level access to named oncall group only, with time-limited ACLs.
- Logging/Proof: enable audit capture that shows request routing, node ids, and storage object locations for the waiver window. TTL logs retained for audit window (default 365 days for exceptions unless legal asks otherwise).
- Telemetry sampling: increase tracing sampling for this tenant (suggestion: 100% for first 48 hours, then 20% baseline).
- Data minimization: reconfigure prefix caching to avoid persisting nonessential PII in transitive caches outside the requested region.

Acceptance criteria for issuing a waiver (example):
- Legal has signed the waiver template (waiver id included) and SLA on retention/erasure is explicit.
- SRE has validated isolation plan in staging and produced a small runbook (see Operator checklist below).
- Telemetry and audit hooks are enabled and tested (test payload showing route + storage id attached to Jira).
- KMS / key location guidance verified or compensating control documented.

Operator checklist (to attach to waiver):
- [ ] Create a temporary routing rule: tenant -> allowed-region (route id), expire_date set.
- [ ] Update ACL for op-group "ds-exceptions-ops-<customer>" and document members.
- [ ] Enable debug tracing for the tenant; run basic end-to-end test (trace id -> saved evidence).
- [ ] Verify that cache TTLs were reduced and confirm no KV snapshots are exported off-region.
- [ ] Create an evidence bundle (see Evidence Packaging section).

Evidence packaging (what to attach to contract & audit):
- Waiver template signed PDF (legal).
- Routing config snapshot (yaml/json), annotated with cluster ids and node hostnames.
- KMS/HSM key metadata showing key location or compensating control note.
- Example trace showing the request path with timestamps (scrub PII if required).
- Operator runbook/execution log showing who enabled/disabled config and at what times (use SSO identity).

Lifecycle and expiration handling:
- All waivers must include a hard expiry date. No implicit renewals.
- 30/14/3 day reminders before expiry automatically created in the waiver Jira ticket; SRE must run a pre-expiry audit checklist at T-14 days.
- If customer requests extension -> reopen triage; treat as new request.

Rollback / emergency deactivation:
- If a region outage or legal red-flag occurs, we must have a fast deactivation path: runbook step to remove temporary routing rule and cut access to associated caches. Maintain a rollback playbook with a dry-run option.
- Post-deactivation steps: run a reconciliation to find any persisted artifacts (snapshots/backups) and schedule erasure if outside customer contract.

Questions for Legal / Open items (working list):
- Can we accept waivers that allow only aggregated analytics outside tenant region but not raw text/PII? (proposal: yes, with data-minimization and hashed-only transfers).
- When a customer uses a partner-managed cloud in a different legal territory, do we require the partner to sign an Addendum? (proposal: yes for EU->non-EU flows).
- Default log retention for exceptions vs standard product logs — confirm with compliance.

Templates (placeholders here):
- Waiver template id: waiver-ds-v1 (use legal to populate).
- Intake Jira: INF-xxxx template: fields: customer, sales-owner, account-id, requested-deviation, justification, start_date, end_date, data-classes, required-controls.
- Evidence bundle naming convention: evidence/<customer>-waiver-<yyyyMMdd>-v1.tar.gz

Low-friction examples (common acceptable patterns):
- Short-term onboarding: 7–14 day temporary processing in a partner region while customer’s anchor is being provisioned. Controls: strict timebox, 100% tracing first 48h, minimal retention.
- Analytics export: aggregated telemetry exported once per week to a centralized analytics region; raw logs never leave pinned region. Controls: aggregation pipeline verification + attested transformation steps.

Example rejected scenarios (fast no):
- Permanent broad permission that allows backups, snapshots or raw logs to be stored permanently outside the pinned region.
- Exceptions without signed waiver or without any audit hooks enabled.

Observability & telemetry notes:
- Create a dedicated dashboard for each active waiver (slo: show routing counts, trace failures, sampling rates, last evidence bundle created).
- Tag traces and logs with "waiver_id" tag. This allows quick extraction for audits.

Communications templates (sales->customer):
- Short acceptance: "We can approve a time-limited exception with the mitigations outlined, with expiry on <date>. Legal will attach the waiver; our SRE team will enable scoped telemetry and provide an evidence bundle on request."
- Rejection: brief reason + alternative mitigation. Avoid technical jargon.

Runbook excerpt (operator):
- Step 1: Obtain waiver id and expiry from Jira ticket INF-1983. Step 2: Create route: rds-create-route --tenant <tid> --dest <region> --expires <date>. Step 3: Enable tracing: tracingctl enable --tenant <tid> --rate 1.0 --note "waiver INF-1983". Step 4: Snapshot evidence: ./collect-evidence.sh --tenant <tid> --waiver INF-1983 -> push to secure-bucket/evidence/<customer>/

Retention and auditability:
- Default evidence retention: 3 years. Exceptions to default retention must be explicit in waiver.
- All operator actions for exceptions must be SSO-authenticated and logged to the audit ledger.

Next steps / actions (owners):
- Legal: produce waiver-ds-v1 template (owner: Priya) — due 2024-10-25.
- SRE: add "waiver_id" tag to tracing platform and make dashboard template (owner: Diego) — due 2024-11-01.
- Platform: create infra PR to add a time-limited routing rule primitive & CLI (owner: Jordan) — PR #214 linked above.

Notes / freeform: 
- This doc should be iterated after 2–3 real waivers: capture what mitigations were costly and which were sufficient.
- Keep waiver window as small as feasible; longer windows require additional controls (multiple approvers, exec sign-off).

Unresolved risks to discuss in weekly sync:
- Third-party subprocessor flows when customer data is processed by a partner in a different legal area.
- Edge-case around subpoena requests for data processed briefly off-region.

If you edit this doc: add your change in a short "changelog" entry at the bottom with date + initials.
